summary: The note compares seasonal seafood harvest calendars and signature dishes on the US East and West coasts. The East features lobster, scallops, shad, bluefish and striped bass, with hearty comforting dishes; the West features Dungeness crab, oysters, King Salmon and halibut, with bolder flavors influenced by Asia and Latin America. It closes by stressing sustainable fishing and naming programs that support responsible seafood choices.
one_line: A comparison of East and West Coast US seasonal seafood calendars, regional dishes, and the importance of sustainable fishing.
key_facts: The note is set on September 26, 2023, as the autumn fishing season gets underway off New England.
New England fisherman John McDermott says autumn brings the best lobster, as cool waters make them plumper and more flavorful, and it is also peak season for Atlantic mackerel.
Chef Emily Park of Boston says the bay scallop season opens in December, and she prepares scallops seared with a simple butter sauce.
Spring on the East Coast brings the shad run, with festivals along rivers like the Connecticut and Hudson; historian Benjamin Thompson describes shad bakes where the fish is cooked whole over a fire.
Summer on the East Coast is the season for bluefish and striped bass; Outer Banks fishing guide Jake Sullivan favors grilled striper with lemon and herbs.
Dungeness crab season in San Francisco typically begins by mid-November, and Chef Lila Ramirez describes crab feeds with garlic butter and sourdough bread.
The Pacific Northwest is known for spot prawns, celebrated for a sweet and delicate taste.

Winter is prime oyster harvest time on the West Coast, with Tomales Bay in California known for its oyster farms; oyster farmer Jeff Larson says colder months yield the firmest and most flavorful oysters.
King Salmon return in spring on the West Coast, a peak called 'Salmon Fever'; Chef and author Kevin Wu says it is celebrated with simple grilling.
Halibut is the summer catch on the West Coast, often served with a bright citrus salsa or atop seasoned grains.
Eastern dishes such as lobster rolls, creamy chowders and clam bakes favor hearty, comforting flavors tied to cold Atlantic waters and colonial history.
Western cuisine is influenced by proximity to Asia and Latin America, with fresh salsas, sushi rolls and wine-infused sauces.
The Monterey Bay Aquarium's Seafood Watch program (West Coast) and the Gulf of Maine Research Institute's sustainable seafood efforts (East Coast) are cited as ways to support responsible harvesting.
